mike: Quick check — following up on the RFC: I want to propose adding a compactness fence to the offload handoff API so receivers can reject mid-compact handoffs. Can we bikeshed the surface and rollout plan?

sara: TL;DR I'm +1 for the fence but worried about API churn for Dedicated customers. Do we have a compatibility strategy?

anand: Can you sketch the minimal change? Is this a new flag on the handoff op or a separate handshake RPC?

mike: Minimal sketch: add optional `compact_fence_id` string to HandOffRequest and a `fence_status` enum on responses. Default empty (no-fence) for compatibility. Example: `{\"compact_fence_id\": \"f-2026-03-22-01\"}`

jia: That seems backwards-compatible. But we need to ensure existing receivers ignore unknown fields (they do), and we should version the protobuf/service to be explicit. Also consider a `fence_ttl` so we can garbage-collect stale fences.

sara: If we push this to hosted customers, we must document behavior when fence is present and receiver doesn't understand it. How about returning 501-like error so caller can fallback?
mike: Plan: 1) protobuf optional field, 2) receiver if unknown -> gracefully accept (no-fence) OR if it understands but fence mismatched -> return `FENCE_REJECT` with reason, 3) handoff caller will treat `FENCE_REJECT` as non-fatal and try alternative pool or compact-wait.

anand: Important tradeoff: if receivers silently accept unknown fence we lose enforcement. We should require server-side deploys to a min-version that understands fences before enabling them in the router. So rollout via feature flag gated on receiver-version.

jia: Agreed. We'll need a router-side release that sends `compact_fence_id` only when the chosen host advertises fence-capability. That's trivial if we add a capability bit in pool metadata.
sara: Ops ask: what's the impact on latency? If we do an extra handshake for fence validation we'll add RTT. Can we piggyback on existing handoff op rather than a separate roundtrip?
mike: The idea is piggybacked. HandOffRequest includes the fence id and receiver validates synchronously when receiving the handoff. No extra network RTT. The validation involves checking compact-in-progress table — local in-memory lookup; should be sub-ms.

anand: Also consider telemetry: add a `hand_off.fence.{accept|reject|unknown}` counter and record `fence_reason` dimension. We can gate high-cardinality reasons behind a flag.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New canary cluster image built: runtime-offload:v2026.3.22-fence. Canary schedule: 2 nodes in prod-canary this afternoon.
sara: Nice. Migration concerns: what about Dedicated where customers pin runtime? We need a deprecation window and explicit opt-in in Console. Suggest: 90-day opt-in before default enabled in hosted.
jia: For private on-prem installs we should provide a migration script that populates `compact_fence_meta` in local DB from existing compaction jobs; otherwise fence will always be unknown and be effectively disabled. We'll add a check in pre-upgrade.
mike: Edge-case: cross-cluster handoffs (router chooses remote pool). If remote pool doesn't support fences, router will either pick another or fall back to best-effort. We need consistent policy—prefer fallback over blocking. Documentable config: `offload.fence_policy = [PREFER_STRICT, FALLBACK, BLOCK]`. Default FALLBACK.
anand: One more: fragmentation regression risk. If we reject handoffs during compaction we may create transient hotspots. We should simulate with the loadgen — create a repro that exercises frequent compaction and handoffs. Can someone own the test?
sara: I'll own the stress test. Plan: spike 10k small-allocation handoffs while compact runs; measure tail latency and failed handoffs.
mike: Thanks. I'll open the follow-up PR: proto + router gating + metrics. Will include a migration note and a console flag for Dedicated.

jia: Small nit: use `compact_fence_id` UUID format and include creation_ts. That helps triage.
mike: Good call. Use `fence-<uuid>-<ts>` format.

anand: After PR, we should schedule a brief arch sync (15m) to walk through the sequence diagrams. I can prep the diagram.
sara: sgtm. One last ask: add automated test asserting that older clients ignoring the field still accept handoff. We can't trust manual QA.
mike: Yep will add unit + integration test. Target to merge by EOD Friday, canary Monday.

ops-bot: incident-bot: NOTICE: Canary scheduled at 2026-03-23T18:00Z for runtime-offload:v2026.3.22-fence on prod-canary-02.

mike: Thanks all — will post PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
